solution: Tyler's answers for the 10-21 wheelchair case. The planes are recorded; paint the interface position and the attachment zones, and set slider ranges, in the answer key editor.
solutionNote: Answer key for the Chihuahua wheelchair case.

params.label: Imported files
params.off: Some of the files are not the ones this case uses. The wheelchair case takes the wheelchair mechanical and solid interfaces.
params.note: The wheelchair Chihuahua's scan, the socket surface cut from it, and the wheelchair mechanical and solid interfaces.

params.label: Scale factor
params.low: Smaller than the notebook's factor, so the socket is built on a shrunken scan and will be tight.
params.high: Larger than this case's factor. At 1.00 the scan is as imported; this case scales it to 0.97 before the socket is built.
params.note: 0.97, this case's scale factor. The scan is shrunk by 3% before the socket is built on it.

params.label: Pelvic plane
params.off: Not the plane this case uses. It sits on the Y maximum face of the attachment surface, looking back along -Y.
params.note: X centroid, Y maximum, Z centroid, with the normal pointing back along -Y.
params.acceptText: Y maximum, normal along Y (either way)

params.label: Interface plane
params.off: Not the face the wheelchair mount sits on. On the wheelchair interface it is the Z maximum face, with the normal along -Z.
params.note: X centroid, Y centroid, Z maximum on the wheelchair interface, with the normal along -Z.
params.acceptText: X centroid · Y centroid · Z maximum, normal along Z (either way)
